commands.author: clawsweeper[bot]
commands.review_summary:
The PR adds strict ALB verified-email admission, a default-on Slack deployment mode with FakeCo locked off, terminal queued-delivery handling when Slack is disabled, and unauthenticated ALB logout cookie clearing across infrastructure, runtime, tests, UI, and documentation.

Reproducibility: yes. for the code-level defects: focused tests and source inspection establish the identity-claim and queued-delivery paths with high confidence. The real AWS control-plane behavior has not been reproduced.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] The sole confirmed repair is a one-line release-policy cleanup that automation can perform without changing behavior.

target.title: Harden FakeCo auth, Slack-off mode, and ALB logout
target.body:
## Summary

- Require the signed ALB identity assertion to contain exactly one verified-email value. Boolean `true` and Cognito UserInfo's exact string `"true"` are accepted; false, missing, invalid, duplicate, and conflicting multi-values fail closed.
- Add a canonical `SlackMode` deployment path. The locked FakeCo profile starts with Slack off, omits Slack secret injection, closes both Slack ingress paths at the ALB and application boundaries, terminally fails already queued delivery without an outbound request, reports the integration as not configured, and requires no placeholder credentials.
- Add a console logout path that expires the configured ALB session cookie plus every supported shard, then redirects to an unauthenticated no-store landing page.
- Update the FakeCo workflow summary, deployment/architecture/product/validation documentation, console state text, and changelog.

## Compatibility and security

The generic AWS template defaults Slack to on, preserving existing Slack-enabled installations and their API/configuration behavior. FakeCo alone locks the initial canary to off; enabling it later requires a reviewed profile change and real sandbox credentials.

Logout ends the ALB session but cannot revoke an upstream identity-provider session. Provider-specific global or front-channel logout remains an installation concern.

## Validation

Tested commit: `87068b32a5d13a92a6ad3d506fa4c7533b4bb993`
Tested tree: `fe2362b5621ec9426c1664952810b87c50264d6e`

- Focused auth/config/FakeCo/HTTP contract: 36 passed.
- Focused HTTP suite after final fixture cleanup: 10 passed.
- Focused production-runtime workerd regression: four tests passed. It completes a queued turn with Slack explicitly off and stale credentials present; a retryable outbound trap makes any leaked post fail the assertion.
- `pnpm check`: 156 core tests passed; 20 Worker tests passed; 53 AWS tests passed with four pre-existing database-backed skips. Type checks, bundles, syntax checks, and Worker dry-run passed.
- Source-blind behavior validation: four clauses passed, including varied verified-email inputs, tampered-render rejection, Slack-off with stale-looking credentials, and cookie-shard/logout behavior.
- Canonical autoreview: clean, no accepted or actionable findings.
- Public Model Identifier Gate: PASS. The candidate adds no model identifier to the public diff or PR proof; build, generated-render, and test-log candidates were audited with no unknowns.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

## Live AWS gap

No AWS, Cognito, ALB, ECS, CloudFormation, GitHub Environment, secret, or deployment mutation was performed for this PR. Deployment-specific proof must still verify the real Cognito claim shape, unauthenticated logout rule and cookie clearing, Slack-off task definition and routes, authenticated state, and later Slack transition before claiming the FakeCo environment live.

## Maintainer proof decision

Repository maintainer @steipete explicitly accepts automated-only confidence for this repository-only landing and owns the residual risk that real ALB, Cognito, or stack-update behavior could differ from the automated harness. This does not waive deployment-specific proof: live AWS validation remains mandatory before dispatching the FakeCo deployment or claiming the environment live.

## Maintainer changelog decision

Repository maintainer @steipete intentionally retains the Unreleased changelog entry. This is a maintainer-authored user-facing fix, the requested scope explicitly requires a changelog update, and repository policy requires changelog coverage for user-facing fixes; it is not contributor-owned release assembly.
